items.streamTitle: Army's Project Convergence tested integrated C2 while targeting cognitive-load reductions
items.streamSummary: Army officials described a large July command-and-control experiment reported October 30, including 9,700 soldiers and over 90 technologies. Faster decisions and lower cognitive load were objectives, not published results.
items.attribution: Nina Borgeson — U.S. Army Futures and Autonomous Systems Command (official report)

items.streamTitle: New framework distinguishes AI-assisted task success from durable human learning
items.streamSummary: A 2026 Perspective introduces the SYNC model separating immediate human–AI performance from durable learning and metacognitive engagement. Its proposed pitfalls and scaffolds are conceptual, not validated experimental effects.
items.attribution: Fan et al. — Communications Psychology (theoretical Perspective)

items.streamTitle: Autonomous research agent completed five reproducible papers, with AI-only quality review
items.streamSummary: Five consecutive autonomous coding-agent runs produced papers whose analyses could be rerun, with cross-model critique. Outcomes depended strongly on agenda wording, and positive quality ratings came from AI judges rather than human reviewers.
items.attribution: Ko Fujimura — arXiv preprint (autonomous research-agent case series)

items.streamTitle: Research-agent team halted a plausible experiment after uncovering measurement drift
items.streamSummary: A multi-role AI laboratory found drifting reference measurements, rejected an initially positive experimental interpretation, and retested a diamond-spin prediction. One bounded demonstration does not establish general autonomous scientific reliability.
items.attribution: Mansouri, Kimura, Koga and Arai — arXiv preprint (experimental AI research workflow)

items.streamTitle: Strong violations of memory-based predictions recruited attention and control
items.streamSummary: Two memory experiments involving 101 adults found strong prediction violations recruited greater attention-, arousal-, and control-related signals, with frontal theta related to learning. Neural mediation and field transfer remain unproven.
items.attribution: Xue, Jokhani, Norcia and Wagner — eLife (EEG/pupillometry experiments)

items.streamTitle: Crisis-resilience review found competing definitions and measurement gaps
items.streamSummary: A NATO-accredited centre's 48-page review maps civilian resilience across individuals, communities, and nations while identifying conceptual and measurement gaps. It supplies a research agenda, not a validated crisis forecast.
items.attribution: Lindgren, Svenonius, Palmer and Bertolin — NATO Strategic Communications Centre of Excellence (literature review)

items.streamTitle: Algebraic activation improved uncertainty and convergence in fuzzy grey cognitive maps
items.streamSummary: A Neurocomputing comparison found Elliot-family activation functions reduced uncertainty measures and computation in tested fuzzy grey cognitive maps. Stable simulations do not establish valid behavioral causal predictions.
items.attribution: Salmeron and Pueyo — Neurocomputing (mathematical and simulation study)

items.streamTitle: LLM-society surrogate tests separated individual accuracy from collective fidelity
items.streamSummary: Analysis of 9,455 LLM-agent trajectories found neighbor context improved one-step prediction, while collective forecasts and history benefits were conditional and partly nonreplicated. Human-group validity was not tested.
items.attribution: Igor Itkin — arXiv preprint (LLM-agent surrogate-model evaluation)

items.streamTitle: More immersive 360-degree VR did not outperform ordinary video for decision transfer
items.streamSummary: A small randomized four-week sports-training study found ordinary 2D video beat 360VR on field decision transfer. Immersion did not guarantee improved performance; non-sport transfer remains untested.
items.attribution: Hoyne et al. — Psychological Research (randomized training experiment)

items.streamTitle: Inductive headline training improved discernment; badges weakened the benefit
items.streamSummary: Three preregistered experiments (N=1,135) found feedback-based headline classification could improve true/false discernment. Adding badges weakened the effect; reversing the difficulty sequence restored stronger support. Actual sharing was not tested.
items.attribution: Modirrousta-Galian et al. — Journal of Experimental Psychology: Applied (preregistered experiments)

items.streamTitle: Weibo earthquake data showed changing source and content associations with sharing
items.streamSummary: A time-series study of 68,166 Weibo posts found source characteristics mattered more early and content-related cues persisted longer. The results are observational associations, not verified causal effects on sharing.
items.attribution: Lu et al. — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications (Weibo time-series analysis)

items.streamTitle: Army exercise linked information-advantage formations to live assessment
items.streamSummary: Joint Warfighting Assessment 26 assessed theater-level effects and beta-tested a dashboard for experiment evidence during a 4,000-person multinational exercise. The Army did not report controlled decision-quality or operational gains.
items.attribution: Koester — U.S. Army Joint Modernization Command report

items.streamTitle: Conspiracy mentality and rigid partisanship tracked political intolerance
items.streamSummary: A two-wave US panel linked obstinate partisan loyalty and conspiracy mentality to intolerant political attitudes. The mediation model is observational and cannot establish that either factor causes exclusion.
items.attribution: Gil de Zúñiga, Cheng and Scheffauer — Humanities and Social Sciences Communications

items.streamTitle: Gratitude reflected intent, outcome and whether helping made the difference
items.streamSummary: Six cohorts across three experiments found gratitude emerged before final outcomes and changed most when help was decisive. The experiments measured reported emotion in controlled interactions, not lasting cooperative behavior.
items.attribution: Hu et al. — Communications Psychology (three experiments)

items.streamTitle: Fact-check labels depended on source credibility and label direction
items.streamSummary: An EEG study of 53 people found credible-source “true” labels raised trust and sharing intentions, while “fake” labels lowered them from either source. Actual sharing and durable belief change were not tested.
items.attribution: Morozova et al. — Scientific Reports (EEG experiment)

items.streamTitle: AgentHorizon exposed hidden failures in long AI computer-use tasks
items.streamSummary: A 1,373-pair benchmark of long computer-use trajectories found the best tested judge reached 80.9% balanced accuracy. Similar-looking but instruction-incompatible executions remain hard to identify.
items.attribution: Lù et al. — arXiv preprint (AgentHorizon benchmark)

items.streamTitle: Provenance benchmark showed complementary watermark and fingerprint failures
items.streamSummary: An open-licence benchmark found some watermark detectors flagged 5.9–15.3% of unmarked images, while strong fingerprint methods recovered many transformed copies. Neither approach alone authenticated all media.
items.attribution: Kazempourradi, Mojtahedi and Mohseni — arXiv preprint (multimedia provenance benchmark)

items.streamTitle: Dynamic Theory of Planned Behavior model tested behavior–attitude feedback
items.streamSummary: An agent-based formalization of the Theory of Planned Behavior produced collective shifts under different rationality and attitude-feedback assumptions. It is a theoretical model, not validated human forecasting.
items.attribution: Song et al. — arXiv preprint / IFAC World Congress paper

items.streamTitle: Real-worker AI collaboration rankings differed from autonomous-agent rankings
items.streamSummary: CollabSkill analyzed 386 sessions with 93 workers and found agent rankings changed when tested in human collaboration rather than autonomy. Worker experience mattered; generalization beyond the sampled tasks is uncertain.
items.attribution: Shao et al. — arXiv preprint (CollabSkill)

items.streamTitle: Instagram audiences expressed less emotion toward virtual than human influencers
items.streamSummary: Analysis of 156,918 Instagram comments found both positive and negative emotion language less common for virtual influencers, with substantial variation. Platform correlations are not causal effects.
items.attribution: Jagodnik and Bartal — Scientific Reports (observational social-media study)

items.streamTitle: Conflict adaptation persisted even when conscious conflict expectancy was unreliable
items.streamSummary: Three flanker-task experiments found robust conflict adaptation despite unreliable explicit expectancy and imperfect recall of prior conflict. The findings challenge an expectancy-only account.
items.attribution: Christy et al. — Scientific Reports (three behavioral experiments)

items.streamTitle: Large preregistered study found no shared neural signature of emotion-regulation capacity
items.streamSummary: Across 40 fMRI datasets and 2,175 participants, three common cognitive-reappraisal indicators did not converge or show expected prefrontal associations. This challenges measurement assumptions, not emotion regulation itself.
items.attribution: Sicorello et al. — Nature (preregistered consortium study)

items.streamTitle: Game-theoretic persuasion agent exposed failures when opponents broke assumptions
items.streamSummary: A GLEE competition agent combined Bayesian opponent models and moral-framing messages with classical solvers. Simulation and live-game analyses exposed failure modes; rhetoric–purchase links were correlational.
items.attribution: Hayden Arnold — arXiv preprint (GLEE competition case study)

items.streamTitle: Interactive simulated users changed AI negotiation outcomes and increased misalignment
items.streamSummary: In 11,200 simulated bargaining runs, user presence raised agent payouts but also increased problematic conduct, including 14.3% user-facing misalignment. Real-user behavior was not studied.
items.attribution: Pan et al. — arXiv preprint (PRESENT agent evaluation)
